title: Completion of a power-multiplicative normed algebra over completed scalars
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, let $H=\widehat F$ be its metric completion [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion], and let $A$ be a nonzero commutative unital $F$-algebra. Suppose $n:A\to\mathbf R_{\ge0}$ satisfies $n(a)=0\Longleftrightarrow a=0$, $n(1)=1$, $n(-a)=n(a)$, $n(a+b)\le\max(n(a),n(b))$, $n(ab)\le n(a)n(b)$, $n(ca)=|c|n(a)$ for $c\in F$, and $n(a^m)=n(a)^m$ for every integer $m\ge1$. Form $\widehat A$ from the Cauchy sequences for $d(a,b)=n(a-b)$, identifying two sequences when their difference tends to zero. Then $\widehat n([(a_j)])=\lim_j n(a_j)$ is well defined and definite. Termwise ring operations and $[(c_j)]\cdot[(a_j)]=[(c_ja_j)]$, for Cauchy sequences $(c_j)$ in $F$, make $\widehat A$ a complete commutative unital $H$-algebra. Its norm satisfies the same normalization, negation, strong triangle, submultiplication and positive-power identities, and $\widehat n(hx)=|h|_H\widehat n(x)$ for $h\in H$. The map $A\to\widehat A$ given by constant sequences is an isometric $F$-algebra embedding with dense image. No finiteness, multiplicativity of $n$, or completeness of $F$ is assumed.

from.place: Historical analytic input supporting the normalization chain from lem-trf-local-term-locality, through Temkin Theorem 3.5.5 Step 2: Distinguished presentations of reduced affinoids over an algebraically closed field. This is below the node level, not a replacement of the current contracting-correspondence unit proof. Supporting analytic lemma in the presentation construction: Norm-preserving lifts for a Tate epimorphism surjective on canonical reductions. Independent analytic input: Finite affinoid maps are finite on spectral unit balls over an algebraically closed field. Proof input: Orthogonal spectral norm on the fraction field of a finite affinoid domain. Supporting input: Stability of the Gauss fraction field of a Tate algebra. BGR stability proof input: Sections 5.3.3–5.3.4, especially Proposition 5.3.3/3 and the conclusion of Section 5.3.4, printed pp.215 and 218–220 (scan PDF pp.221 and 224–226); Section 5.3.4 removes the divisible-value-group restriction. Supporting input for the present split: Proposition 5.3.3/2, printed pp.214–215 (scan PDF pp.220–221). Supporting input for Proposition 5.3.3/2: Proposition 5.3.3/2, printed p.215 (scan PDF p.221), norm-completion diagram and the two spectral inequalities; Theorems 3.2.1/2 and 3.2.2/2. General completion input: extending both the normed algebra and its scalar field before forming the finite scalar envelope.
